# -h shows the usage, and -version the version. A build for development
# has no version.
exec rexdiff -h
stderr '^usage: rexdiff \[flags\] \[repo\]'
exec rexdiff -version
stdout '^\(devel\)$'

# rexdiff does not start when its input is wrong. Each error says what is
# wrong, and which values are allowed.
! exec rexdiff -layout sideways
stderr 'invalid value "sideways" for flag -layout: expected one of unified, split'
! exec rexdiff $WORK
stderr '^rexdiff: open .+: git rev-parse: fatal: not a git repository'
exec git init -q repo
! exec rexdiff repo -wrap=false
stderr '^rexdiff: unknown argument -wrap=false \(flags go before the repo\)$'
! exec rexdiff -config '{"layuot": "split"}' repo
stderr '^rexdiff: config: unknown key "layuot"$'

# -check checks the settings without a repository, for the Rex action.
! exec rexdiff -check -config '{"layout": "sideways"}'
stderr '^rexdiff: config: invalid value for layout: expected one of unified, split, not "sideways"$'
exec rexdiff -check -config '{"layout": "split"}'
! stderr .
